title: The Ass Carrying the Image
text:
A donkey was given an important job. It was to carry a famous wooden statue of a god through the streets of a city to the temple where the image would be installed.

As the procession passed, crowds lined the streets. People bowed low, knelt and pressed their hands together in reverence. The donkey looked around and drew its own conclusion: all this respect was for him. He lifted his head, swelled with importance and soon decided that a creature so honored should not have to keep walking. He planted his hooves and refused to take another step.

The driver did not share his view. He brought the stick down hard on the donkey's back and told him plainly that people had not yet started worshipping donkeys. The bows were for the god he was carrying. The donkey, sore and corrected, went on to the temple.
lesson: When people defer to you because of your position, the respect belongs to the role, not to you. Keep carrying the load, and you will be less surprised on the day the role passes to someone else.
people: A donkey, its driver, the crowd
